title: Redshift: nodes, distribution keys, sort keys and Serverless

videos.script: Every night Quitanda wants the same report. Sales per store per day, over the whole year. {{report}} A database built to fetch one order by its id is slow at that. A warehouse is built for it. {{warehouse}} Redshift spreads the rows over many slices and reads only the columns a query names. {{slices}} Where each row goes is a decision you write in the table's definition. Get it wrong and one slice does half the work while the others wait. {{skew}} The order the rows are written in decides how many blocks a query can skip. {{sortkeys}} moto records a cluster and runs no SQL, so you will measure both effects with two small models. {{models}} Then the bill. A cluster costs every hour it exists. Serverless costs every hour it works. You will find the number of busy hours a day where one becomes cheaper than the other. {{bill}}
